issues.title: A version update deactivates the row until the process restarts
issues.summary: Cordis/Node cache modules by resolved path, so a running process may keep the old module while the profile gains new config keys. resolveConfig now warns and ignores unknown keys, preventing future config-first updates from deactivating the row.
evidence: GOOD: GET /api/dsh-turbo/health -> 200 with version 0.1.0 before the update
BAD:  GET /api/dsh-turbo/health -> 401 after the profile recomposed with the 0.2.1 patch
config keys in cordis.patch.yml known only to 0.2.1: maxReasoningEffort, defaultGear
fixed: src/host/plugin.ts resolveConfig accepts an onUnknown callback and continues with known keys
fixed: apply logs ignored keys through the Cordis logger
issues.impact: The user sees the feature vanish after updating and cannot tell a crash from a disabled plugin.

recommendation.action: Done: unknown keys are warned and ignored, while invalid values for known keys still fail loudly.

issues.workaround: One restart is still required to load this fix into a process already running the older module.

issues.title: No reproducible end-to-end speedup has been demonstrated
issues.summary: Two interleaved 20-task sweeps produced opposite signs at the median (-35% in sweep 1, +12% in sweep 2), and task-level deltas ranged -78% to +257%. The composition mounts no optional stage Turbo can remove, so the policy only nudges model behaviour.
evidence: PERFORMANCE.md section 2 (sweep 1): turbo median 28 952 ms vs default 44 636 ms, turbo 7/9 passed vs default 9/9
PERFORMANCE.md section 3 (sweep 2): turbo median 33 638 ms vs default 29 980 ms, turbo 19/20 passed vs default 18/19
benchmark/smoke-three-arm-keep.md: single task, fast -8.3%, max -9.2%
benchmark/paired-ui-sample.json: one paired UI sample, -29.2%, different task, single run, token figure includes cache reads
PERFORMANCE.md section 4.3: sum-js repeat 3 passed 9/9; Fast median +32.4% slower, Max median -8.9% but mean +16.8% slower
PERFORMANCE.md section 4.3: multi-file complete pair had Fast +10.2% and Max +22.4%; Max passed only 2/4 runs
issues.impact: Any published multiplier would be unsupported. The honest positioning is 'switchable, observable execution preference'.

recommendation.action: Run --repeat 3 or higher over a larger task set before making any speed claim; report pass rate next to latency.

issues.workaround: Keep Turbo OFF by default (current defaultMode: default) and let users decide per session.

issues.title: The fast and max gears currently select the same reasoning effort
issues.summary: Fast now uses low effort and Max uses high effort. The gears remain different in policy text and now also select distinct request effort.
evidence: cordis.patch.yml: reasoningEffort: low
fixed: cordis.patch.yml sets maxReasoningEffort: high
fixed: scripts/benchmark.mjs pins Fast=low and Max=high through the same plugin config
issues.impact: Three-arm results overstate the difference between gears; the 'max' arm is not a stronger-reasoning arm.

recommendation.action: Done: maxReasoningEffort is high and the benchmark patch preserves the distinction.

issues.workaround: None. Re-run the three-arm benchmark because earlier Fast/Max numbers used equal effort.

issues.title: The reasoning-effort lever is applied but its effect is not observable in metrics
issues.summary: The request header really does carry the configured effort (verified after the prepend fix), yet every arm reports reasoningTokens 0, so nothing proves the lever reduces thinking or latency.
evidence: session log request/header config: {"provider":"deepseek-official","model":"deepseek-flash","reasoningEffort":"low"}
benchmark/smoke-three-arm-keep.md: reasoning tok = 0 for default, fast and max
evidence.jsonl confirms Max reasoningEffort=high on every pre-step, but formal-sum-js-3x still reports reasoningTokens=0 for all 9 runs
issues.impact: The plugin's strongest latency lever is an assumption, not a measurement.

recommendation.action: Find a proxy metric that actually moves (output tokens, first-token latency, or wall clock on a reasoning-heavy task), or confirm the provider reports reasoning usage at all.

issues.workaround: Compare wall clock and output tokens, not reasoningTokens.

issues.title: Verification detection recognises commands, not outcomes
issues.summary: The 'verification ran' metric matches shell command text against test/build/lint patterns. It proves a command was attempted, never that it succeeded, and it is presented next to metrics that do imply outcomes.
evidence: src/host/metrics.ts VERIFICATION_COMMAND regex
src/host/metrics.ts looksLikeVerification() is driven by tool/call arguments only
UI row label: 'Verification ran' / '是否执行了测试'
issues.impact: A user can read 'verification: yes' as 'tests passed'.

recommendation.action: Keep the label as an observation and state it in the UI tooltip and README ('a command was attempted, not that it passed').

issues.workaround: Read the session log's tool/result isError for outcome.

issues.title: In-flight turns are invisible in the metrics panel
issues.summary: Session metrics summarise completed turns only, so during the first or current turn the panel shows 'turns 0' and dashes.
evidence: src/host/metrics.ts summary() returns nulls when no completed record exists
Live probe during an active turn returned turns=0, all metrics null
issues.impact: Cosmetic confusion; looks like metrics are broken on a fresh session.

recommendation.action: Expose the live turn (mode, steps so far, elapsed) separately from completed-turn aggregates.

issues.title: The toggle polls the bridge every 2.5 s
issues.summary: Cross-tab convergence is achieved by polling plus the revision guard rather than a pushed event.
evidence: src/client/turbo-toggle.tsx POLL_MS = 2500
src/host/plugin.ts revision guard returns 409 on a stale write
issues.impact: Negligible on loopback; unnecessary traffic in principle.

recommendation.action: Only worth fixing with a gateway event; keep polling until then.

issues.title: Narrow-screen layout is only guarded by CSS
issues.summary: A media query collapses the ON label to the bolt glyph below 640 px, but it has not been verified in a real narrow window.
evidence: src/client/turbo-toggle.tsx TURBO_CSS @media (max-width:640px)
issues.impact: Possible overlap with the model selector on very narrow composers.

recommendation.action: Verify at ~380 px composer width and screenshot it.

issues.title: Only DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 was actually exercised
issues.summary: The manifest declares dsh.engines >=0.2.0-rc.1 and marks 0.2.0-rc.2 as tested; every other version is an unverified claim. The plugin leans on observed, not documented, shapes (slot names, hook payload fields, asar layout).
evidence: package.json dsh.engines + dsh.compatibility
compatibility-report.md sections 2 and 3 cite source lines from 0.2.0-rc.2 only
tests/compatibility.test.mjs encodes 0.2.0-rc.2 facts
issues.impact: A DSH upgrade can break the plugin in ways no current test predicts.

recommendation.action: Run the compatibility suite against each release before widening the declared range.

issues.workaround: Pin the DSH version in deployments.

issues.title: install.ps1 crashed under Windows PowerShell 5.1
issues.summary: Four defects: $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path is empty inside a param() default; app.asar was treated as a directory; a GUI-subsystem executable was not awaited so $LASTEXITCODE was unset; non-ASCII bullets were mis-decoded as ANSI.
evidence: before: Split-Path : cannot bind argument to parameter 'Path' because it is null (install.ps1:33)
before: 'npm add failed with exit code ' with an empty code
before: mojibake 鈥? instead of bullet glyphs
after: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/install.ps1 -Profile desktop -> exit 0
after: both scripts parse with 0 errors and contain 0 non-ASCII characters
issues.impact: Installation and update appeared broken on the default Windows shell.

recommendation.action: Done: resolve defaults after binding, test the asar file, prefer pnpm and verify from the profile manifest, ASCII + UTF-8 BOM output, health probe with retries.

issues.title: An unsupported reasoning effort could fail entire turns
issues.summary: The shipped DeepSeek Messages adapter accepts only off|low|high|max. A configured 'minimal' made every Turbo turn end with UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT before the self-healing path existed.
evidence: before: dsh: UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT: provider "deepseek-official" model "deepseek-flash" does not support reasoning effort "minimal"
adapter source: dsh-llm-deepseek accepted set [off, low, high, max]
after: agent/request-error handler disables the lever for that agent and returns { kind: 'retry' }
after: probe with reasoningEffort low -> request/header carries low, run exits 0
issues.impact: A configuration mistake used to be fatal per turn; now it degrades and is reported.

recommendation.action: Done: route refusal disables the lever, writes an effort-disabled evidence line, and the capability row explains it.

issues.workaround: Keep reasoningEffort at 'inherit' until a route-supported value is chosen.

issues.title: Bare pnpm audit/issues commands ran package-manager commands instead of the issue gate
issues.summary: pnpm reserves both audit and issues. Package scripts with those names require pnpm run, while the bare commands reported dependency or repository information and never validated audit/issues.json.
evidence: observed: pnpm audit printed 'No known vulnerabilities found' without rendering audit/ISSUES.md
observed: pnpm issues printed the repository Issues URL without rendering audit/ISSUES.md
fixed: package scripts are named check:issues and check:issues:strict
verified: pnpm run check:issues runs check-issues.mjs and refreshes the Markdown view
issues.impact: A developer could believe the machine-readable issue registry passed when it was never checked.

recommendation.action: Done: use pnpm run check:issues for validation/rendering and pnpm run check:issues:strict for the high-severity gate.

issues.workaround: Use node scripts/check-issues.mjs directly on older checkouts.
